headline: A French cheese is named the best in the world

sources.title: World Cheese Awards: French 24-month Comté named world's best cheese (CNN)
World Cheese Awards Supreme Champion announced (Retail Times)
French Comté named world's best cheese at 2026 awards (The Connexion)

chunks.text: On November 12, 2026, judges at the World Cheese Awards in Cordoba, Spain, named a hard French cheese called Comté the best in the world. It comes from the Jura Mountains of eastern France. The winner was [[aged]] for 24 months, kept on a shelf so its taste grew stronger. It {{stood out}} among 5,330 cheeses from 45 countries. It was aged in an old [[fort]] by a [[family business]] that started in 1907 and has been {{passed down}} ever since.

verbs.correct: To be easy to notice as the best
verbs.wrong: To be cut into equal pieces
verbs.why: His work stands out from the rest of the class. One singer always stands out in the school choir. The Comté stood out among 5,330 cheeses from 45 countries.

verbs.correct: To give something to younger family members
verbs.wrong: To fill something with milk and water
verbs.why: Families often pass down old recipes to their children. Some parents pass down their small shop to a son or daughter. The business that aged the Comté has been passed down through the family since 1907.

chunks.text: Experts judged the cheeses on taste, smell, look and [[texture]]. The best cheeses from each judging table {{moved on}} to a second [[round]]. Then 14 top judges each chose one favorite for a live final [[on stage]]. That {{narrowed the list down}} to 14 cheeses. The winning cheese was the favorite of one judge, a Spanish cheese expert. He said its [[flavor]] changes in the mouth, with [[layers]] of [[nutty]] taste.

verbs.correct: To reach the next part of a contest
verbs.wrong: To share a table with others
verbs.why: The top two teams move on to the final. Only the fastest runners move on to the next race. The best cheeses from each table moved on to a second round.

verbs.correct: To make a list shorter by removing some
verbs.wrong: To make a list in order of size
verbs.why: She narrows down her list of colleges to three. The coach narrows the team down to 20 players. The choices of the 14 top judges narrowed the list down to 14 cheeses.

chunks.text: In the final, each judge gave every cheese a score out of seven. The contest {{came down to}} three cheeses. All three {{racked up}} the same [[total]] of 81 points. The other two were a Swiss mountain cheese and a French cheese made from [[sheep's milk]]. The judges used a [[tiebreaker]], a rule for choosing a winner when scores are equal. The Jura cheese {{edged out}} the other two.

verbs.correct: To end with only a small number left
verbs.wrong: To be moved to a bigger stage
verbs.why: The cooking contest often comes down to two chefs. The race comes down to two runners at the end. The contest came down to three cheeses.

verbs.correct: To collect a number of points
verbs.wrong: To send a gift to each judge
verbs.why: Good players rack up points fast. Our team often racks up 30 points in a game. All three cheeses in the final racked up the same total of 81 points.

verbs.correct: To win by a very small amount
verbs.wrong: To ask for a new vote
verbs.why: Our team edges out the other school by one point. She often edges out older runners at the finish. The Jura cheese edged out the other two cheeses on a tiebreaker.

chunks.text: The event's host, a cheese writer, {{pointed out}} its dark [[golden]] color. He said long aging helps {{bring out}} flavor. The cheese is made from [[raw milk]], milk that has not been heated to kill [[germs]]. The U.S. has strict rules on raw-milk cheese from other countries because of [[health concerns]]. Cheese aged for more than 60 days, like this one, can still be sold there. Each [[wheel]] takes two years to make, so [[supplies]] may {{run out}} quickly.

verbs.wrong: To change the color of something
verbs.why: The guide points out old paintings on the walls. My teacher points out small mistakes in my writing. The host pointed out the dark golden color of the Comté.

verbs.correct: To make a taste stronger and clearer
verbs.wrong: To keep a cheese fresh and soft
verbs.why: A little salt brings out the sweetness of the tomatoes. Fresh herbs bring out the taste of the soup. The host said long aging helps bring out the flavor of a cheese.

verbs.correct: To be all gone, with none left
verbs.why: The free tickets often run out in an hour. Water supplies sometimes run out in a dry summer. Each wheel takes two years to make, so supplies of the winning cheese may run out quickly.

ex: The store cuts each wheel into small pieces.
A whole wheel of cheese can weigh 90 pounds.
They keep every wheel on a wooden shelf.

mainIdea.s: Judges at a world contest in Spain picked a French cheese aged for two years as the best of more than 5,000 entries. It won a close final on a tiebreaker after three cheeses got equal scores.
mainIdea.why: The Comté stood out among 5,330 cheeses. Three cheeses racked up 81 points, and it edged out the others on a tiebreaker.

mainIdea.s: A hard French cheese from the mountains took the top prize at a big contest held in Cordoba. The judges said it won easily, with a much higher score than the Swiss and sheep's milk cheeses.
mainIdea.why: Close, but it did not win easily. All three cheeses in the final racked up the same total, so the judges needed a tiebreaker.

mainIdea.s: France has asked American officials to ease their rules on raw-milk cheese from Europe. Farmers in the Jura say their sales have dropped because many wheels are stopped at busy U.S. ports.
mainIdea.why: This is about a French Comté named the world's best cheese. It came down to three cheeses, and the Comté won on a tiebreaker.

tf.s: A French Comté stood out among thousands of cheeses at the awards.
tf.why: Judges at the World Cheese Awards in Spain chose it from 5,330 cheeses from 45 countries.

tf.s: The winning cheese was aged for only a few weeks.
tf.why: It was aged for 24 months. The host said long aging helps bring out flavor.

tf.s: Three cheeses racked up the same score in the final.
tf.why: Each of them got a total of 81 points, so the judges used a tiebreaker.

tf.s: The Comté edged out the others with a higher total score.
tf.why: It had the same total of 81 points as the other two cheeses. It won only on a tiebreaker.

tf.s: The cheese comes from a business passed down through one family.
tf.why: The family business started in 1907 and has been passed down through the family since then.

tf.s: The Comté is made from milk that has been heated to kill germs.
tf.why: It is made from raw milk, which is not heated. The host pointed out that it gets its dark color from time, not heat.

lines.text: Did you hear a French cheese was named the best in the world?
A Comté from the Jura Mountains. It {{stood out}} among more than 5,000 cheeses.
Wow. Stop, that [[makes my mouth water]].
Here's the fun part. It sat on a shelf for two years before the contest.
Two years? I guess [[good things come to those who wait]].
Exactly. The host said long aging helps {{bring out}} the flavor.
So how did the judges pick it?
Each of the 14 top judges chose one favorite. Then the final {{came down to}} three cheeses.
Not at all. All three {{racked up}} 81 points.
The Comté {{edged out}} the other two on a tiebreaker.
A family business from 1907. It's been {{passed down}} for generations. It's [[a family affair]].
I love that. Can I buy some here?
Maybe, but each wheel takes two years, so it could {{run out}} fast. You might need to [[treat yourself]] soon.
[[I'm sold]]. I'm going to try some this weekend.

expressions.def: Used to say that a food sounds or looks so good you want to eat it
ex: That smell from the kitchen makes my mouth water.
Just the word pizza makes my mouth water.

expressions.expr: good things come to those who wait
expressions.def: Used to say that being patient often brings a good result
ex: The line was long, but good things come to those who wait.

expressions.def: Something that many people in one family do together
ex: The bakery is a family affair, with three sisters and their dad.

expressions.def: Used to tell someone to buy or enjoy something special
ex: You worked hard this week, so treat yourself to a nice dinner.

expressions.def: Used to say that someone has convinced you to want or try something
ex: Free dessert with every meal? I'm sold.
